script.title: Freelance taxes at $30K, $60K and $120K: three real examples
script.hook: How much tax does a freelancer actually pay? The honest answer is: it depends, which isn't useful. segments.heading: Intro
segments.narration: How much tax does a freelancer actually pay? The honest answer is: it depends, which isn't useful. So in this video we'll work through three real examples, start to finish, with twenty twenty-six federal numbers. A freelancer making thirty thousand dollars of profit, one making sixty thousand, and one making a hundred and twenty thousand. All single, no other job, standard deduction. segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. the small paper receipt mascot with a folded corner, round glasses and big eyes standing beside three coin towers of different heights on a navy background. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Profit
segments.narration: First, one word that matters more than any other: profit. Not revenue. If clients paid you seventy thousand and you spent ten thousand on software, equipment, mileage and fees, your profit is sixty thousand. Every number in this video starts from profit. That's also why expenses matter so much, which we'll come back to at the end. If you only know your revenue, stop and add up your expenses first, because otherwise every estimate you make will be too high and you'll overpay all year.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. a funnel turning a wide coin stream into a narrower one. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: The two taxes
segments.narration: Freelancers pay two federal taxes on that profit. The first is self-employment tax, which is Social Security and Medicare. At a job, your employer paid half of it and you never saw that half. Now you pay both halves: fifteen point three percent, on ninety-two point three five percent of your profit. The second is ordinary income tax, using the same brackets as everybody else. Most people only think about the second one. That's the mistake. For most freelancers under about a hundred thousand of profit, self-employment tax is actually the bigger of the two.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. two coin stacks, the coral one taller than the mint one. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Deductions
segments.narration: Before income tax, three things come off. Half of your self-employment tax, as an adjustment. The standard deduction, sixteen thousand one hundred dollars for a single filer in twenty twenty-six. And the qualified business income deduction, which is generally twenty percent of your business income after that adjustment, limited to twenty percent of your taxable income. Those three together are why income tax looks surprisingly low in our examples. Self-employment tax gets none of them, apart from the small adjustment to the profit it's calculated on.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. three small tags peeling off a coin stack. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: $30K
segments.narration: Example one. Thirty thousand dollars of profit. Self-employment tax is about four thousand two hundred forty dollars. Taxable income, after half of that, the standard deduction and the QBI deduction, is about nine thousand four hundred. All of it sits in the ten percent bracket, so income tax is about nine hundred forty dollars. Total federal tax: about five thousand one hundred eighty dollars. That's seventeen percent of profit, and more than eighty percent of it is self-employment tax. This is why people earning thirty thousand from a side business are shocked: they expected almost nothing.

segments.heading: $60K
segments.narration: Example two. Sixty thousand of profit. Self-employment tax is about eight thousand four hundred eighty. Taxable income comes to about thirty-one thousand seven hundred, which reaches into the twelve percent bracket, so income tax is about three thousand five hundred sixty. Total: about twelve thousand thirty-seven dollars, or twenty percent of profit. Notice that someone at this level would say, I'm in the twelve percent bracket. True, and also misleading. Their real federal rate on that profit is twenty percent, before any state tax.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. a medium coin tower, two-thirds coral. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: $120K
segments.narration: Example three. A hundred and twenty thousand of profit. Self-employment tax is about sixteen thousand nine hundred fifty. Taxable income is about seventy-six thousand three hundred, which reaches the twenty-two percent bracket, so income tax is about eleven thousand five hundred. Total: about twenty-eight thousand four hundred sixty, or twenty-four percent of profit. Income tax is catching up with self-employment tax now. And above the Social Security wage base, a hundred eighty-four thousand five hundred of earnings in twenty twenty-six, the twelve point four percent part stops, so the mix changes again at higher incomes.

segments.heading: Next dollar
segments.narration: Here's a number that matters even more for decisions: what your next dollar costs. For our thirty thousand freelancer, an extra thousand dollars of profit adds about two hundred sixteen dollars of federal tax. At sixty thousand, about two hundred thirty-one. At a hundred and twenty thousand, about three hundred five. Flip that around and it's what a thousand dollar deduction saves. So a business expense saves you somewhere between a fifth and a third of its cost. It's never free money, which is why buying things just for the write-off is a bad deal.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. three small coins with slices of different sizes. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Set aside
segments.narration: So how much should each freelancer set aside? Take the federal rate and add your state. With a five percent state tax, that's roughly twenty-two percent at thirty thousand, twenty-five percent at sixty thousand and twenty-nine at a hundred twenty thousand. Round up a little if your income is growing, because the next dollar costs more than the average. Per month, that's roughly four hundred thirty, one thousand and two thousand four hundred dollars of federal tax alone. Move it into a separate savings account the day each client pays, not at the end of the month.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. three jars filling to different levels. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Quarterly
segments.narration: And the quarterly payments? If these were each freelancer's first steady year, the four estimated payments would be roughly thirteen hundred, three thousand and seven thousand one hundred dollars each. If they had a lower tax bill last year, the safe harbor lets them pay a quarter of last year's total tax each time instead, and settle the rest in April. That's legal and common. Just make sure the difference is sitting in savings, because April will ask for it.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. four evenly spaced coin stacks on a timeline. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Married or W-2
segments.narration: What changes if you're married, or have a job as well? If you're married filing jointly and your spouse has little income, the standard deduction doubles to thirty-two thousand two hundred and the brackets are roughly twice as wide, so income tax drops a lot. Self-employment tax doesn't change at all: it's per person, on your own profit. If you or your spouse have a W-2 job, your freelance profit sits on top of that salary, so it's taxed at your higher bracket from the first dollar. That's the most common reason side-hustlers are short in April. Their job withholding covers the job, and nothing covers the side income.

segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. two coin stacks, one stacked on top of a small briefcase. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: State
segments.narration: Then there's your state. Nine states have no broad wage income tax, and the rest range from a few percent to over ten at high incomes. Some cities add their own. Most states with an income tax also expect quarterly estimated payments, often on the same dates as the federal ones, through their own website. Look up your state's rate for your income, add it to the federal percentage, and that's your full set-aside. If you move states during the year, you may file in both, so keep track of the date you moved.

segments.heading: Levers
segments.narration: Three levers move these numbers legally. First, real business expenses with records: mileage at seventy-two and a half cents a mile, or seventy-six from July, software, a home office if you qualify. Second, retirement. A SEP IRA contribution of about eleven thousand dollars would cut our sixty thousand freelancer's federal tax by about a thousand. At a hundred and twenty thousand, a full SEP of around twenty-two thousand saves close to four thousand. Third, health. Self-employed health insurance premiums and HSA contributions lower income tax. None of these reduce self-employment tax except business expenses, which is worth knowing.

segments.heading: Mistakes
segments.narration: And three mistakes that make these bills worse. Using your bracket as your savings rate. Forgetting that nobody withholds tax for you, so you owe it four times a year, not once. And mixing business and personal money, so you can't prove your expenses and end up paying tax on a profit that's higher than it really was. Fix those three and you're ahead of most freelancers.

script.title: Your 1099s explained: every form, every mistake, every fix
script.hook: Over the next few weeks, forms with the number ten ninety-nine on them are going to show up in your mailbox and your inbox. If you're a freelancer, they matter, and they confuse almost everyone. In this video: which forms you can expect, what each one means, why they almost never match your bank account, what to do when one is wrong, what to do when one never arrives, and the forms you might owe other people. Twenty twenty-six rules, filing in twenty twenty-seven. Education, not tax advice. Grab your income log; you'll want it.

segments.heading: Intro
segments.narration: Over the next few weeks, forms with the number ten ninety-nine on them are going to show up in your mailbox and your inbox. If you're a freelancer, they matter, and they confuse almost everyone. In this video: which forms you can expect, what each one means, why they almost never match your bank account, what to do when one is wrong, what to do when one never arrives, and the forms you might owe other people. Twenty twenty-six rules, filing in twenty twenty-seven. Education, not tax advice. Grab your income log; you'll want it.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. the small paper receipt mascot with a folded corner, round glasses and big eyes surrounded by a fan of envelopes on a navy background. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: What a 1099 is
segments.narration: A ten ninety-nine is an information return. It's how a business tells the IRS, and you, that it paid you money that wasn't wages. No tax was withheld. The IRS gets a copy, and its computers match those copies to your tax return. That's the whole point: it's a cross-check. It doesn't create the tax. You owe tax on your freelance profit whether a form arrives or not. And a form arriving doesn't mean you owe tax on every dollar on it, as we'll see.
segments.on_screen_text: An information return, not a bill
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. a form with an arrow to a small IRS-style building silhouette and to a person. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: 1099-NEC
segments.narration: The main one for freelancers is the ten ninety-nine NEC, for nonemployee compensation. A client sends it if they paid you two thousand dollars or more during twenty twenty-six for services, directly, by bank transfer, check or cash. That threshold went up from six hundred dollars this year, so you may get fewer of these than before. It's due to you by February first, twenty twenty-seven, because January thirty-first is a Sunday. Some clients send them by email or through a portal, so check your spam folder and your client dashboards.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. a single form with a small bank icon and a calendar. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: 1099-K
segments.narration: The second is the ten ninety-nine K. Payment platforms send it: card processors, PayPal, Stripe, marketplaces. If a client paid you through one of them, the platform reports it, not the client. That's why a client who paid you by card shouldn't send you a ten ninety-nine NEC for the same money. For twenty twenty-six, platforms have to send one if you passed twenty thousand dollars and two hundred transactions, though some send them at lower amounts. The key thing to know: it shows the gross amount, before fees and refunds.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. a form with a card icon and a coin with a slice taken out. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Others
segments.narration: A few others you might see. A ten ninety-nine MISC for things like rent, royalties or prizes. A ten ninety-nine INT from your bank, for interest, including that high-yield savings account where you keep your tax money. Interest is taxable, so don't forget it. And ten ninety-nine DIV and B forms from a brokerage if you invest. Those brokerage forms often come later, in mid to late February, and sometimes they get corrected. That's one reason not to file on the first possible day.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. four small forms with tiny icons: a house, a piggy bank, a chart. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Why they don't match
segments.narration: Now the big question: why don't your forms match your bank account? Timing is the usual reason. Most freelancers use the cash method, so income counts when you receive it. A client who mailed a check on December thirtieth may put it on their twenty twenty-six form, but if it arrived January fourth, it's twenty twenty-seven income for you. Fees are the next reason: the ten ninety-nine K is gross. Then refunds, chargebacks, reimbursed expenses, and plain mistakes, like someone else's payment on your form.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. two calendar pages with an arrow between them. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: What to report
segments.narration: So what do you report? Your actual business income for the year, from your own income log. Report the gross amount clients paid, and list platform fees as an expense. If your total is lower than the forms add up to, be able to explain why, with records. If your total is higher, that's normal: lots of income comes without a form. The forms are a floor the IRS can see, not the number you have to use.
segments.on_screen_text: Report actual income, from your log
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. a ledger with a mint check mark beside a stack of forms. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Wrong form
segments.narration: When a form is wrong, here's the fix. One: check your own records first, so you know exactly what's wrong. Two: email the payer, say which amount is wrong, what it should be and why, and attach proof, like the bank deposit or the refund. Three: ask for a corrected ten ninety-nine. They file the correction with the IRS as well. Four: if it doesn't arrive by the time you file, report the right amount and keep every email and record. Don't just ignore it, because a mismatch is what triggers IRS letters.
segments.on_screen_text: Check · email · corrected form · keep records
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. a form with a pencil and a paperclip. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Personal 1099-K
segments.narration: A special case: a ten ninety-nine K for personal stuff. Maybe friends paid you back for concert tickets through an app, or you sold your old furniture online. Selling personal items for less than you paid isn't taxable income. Reimbursements from friends aren't income either. Ask the platform to correct it if it's wrong. If they won't, the IRS has instructions on its ten ninety-nine K page for reporting and backing out amounts that aren't income. Keep proof: receipts, order emails and messages.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. a couch with a price tag and a down arrow. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Missing
segments.narration: And when a form never arrives? Nothing changes. You report the income anyway. The two thousand dollar threshold is about when the client has to file, not about when you have to pay tax. A client who paid you fifteen hundred dollars won't send a form, and that fifteen hundred is still income. This is where a simple income log saves you: every payment, every client, with dates.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. an empty mailbox next to a full ledger. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Sending them
segments.narration: Now the other side: you might owe forms to other people. If, in your business, you paid another freelancer or contractor two thousand dollars or more for services in twenty twenty-six, directly by bank transfer or check, you generally need to send them a ten ninety-nine NEC by February first and file it with the IRS. Payments by card or through a platform don't count, because the platform reports them. Get a W-9 from them for their name and taxpayer number. If you haven't, ask today. You can file online through the IRS's free system or through a filing service.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. the small paper receipt mascot with a folded corner, round glasses and big eyes handing a form to another small mascot. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Your ID
segments.narration: A quick word about the information on these forms. Clients ask for a W-9 to get your name and taxpayer number, and that number goes on the ten ninety-nine. If you're a sole proprietor, you can use your Social Security number, but you don't have to. You can get a free employer identification number from the IRS in a few minutes online, even with no employees, and give that to clients instead. Fewer copies of your Social Security number sitting in client inboxes is a good thing. Make sure the name on the W-9 matches the number, or forms can get rejected.
segments.on_screen_text: Use a free EIN on W-9s
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. a W-9 style form with a small shield. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Keep
segments.narration: Finally, keep everything. The forms, your income log, the emails asking for corrections, the bank statements. Generally the IRS has three years from when you file to ask questions, longer in some situations, so keep at least three years and ideally a bit more. A folder per year, on your computer and backed up, is plenty. If a letter ever arrives asking about a mismatch, you'll answer it in ten minutes instead of a week.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. a row of yearly folders with a small lock. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Calendar
segments.narration: Your 1099 calendar, then. This month: look for forms by email and in client portals, and request W-9s from anyone you paid. February first: forms due to you, and forms due from you. February: chase missing or wrong forms and close your books. Late February or March: file, once everything is in. Throughout: your own records come first and the forms are the cross-check.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. a short timeline with four dots. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Recap
segments.narration: Recap: a ten ninety-nine NEC comes from clients who paid you two thousand dollars or more directly. A ten ninety-nine K comes from platforms and shows gross amounts. They rarely match your bank, and that's fine if your records explain it. Wrong form? Ask for a correction and keep proof. Missing form? Report the income anyway. And if you paid contractors, send yours by February first. The Quarterly Tax Tracker in the description has an income log built for exactly this. Subscribe for one freelancer money move a week.

script.hook: There are dozens of lists of freelancer tax write-offs. Most of them treat a twenty dollar notebook and a twenty thousand dollar retirement contribution as if they're the same thing. So in this video we'll rank the common deductions by what they're actually worth, using a freelancer with sixty thousand dollars of profit and twenty twenty-six federal numbers. We'll also cover the rules that make each one stick if you're ever asked. Education, not tax advice. And at the end, the things people try to deduct that don't count.

Most of them treat a twenty dollar notebook and a twenty thousand dollar retirement contribution as if they're the same thing. So in this video we'll rank the common deductions by what they're actually worth, using a freelancer with sixty thousand dollars of profit and twenty twenty-six federal numbers. We'll also cover the rules that make each one stick if you're ever asked. Education, not tax advice. And at the end, the things people try to deduct that don't count.

segments.heading: How much
segments.narration: First, the exchange rate. At sixty thousand of profit, single, every thousand dollars of business expenses saves about two hundred thirty-one dollars of federal tax, because it lowers both self-employment tax and income tax. Some deductions only lower income tax, like retirement contributions and health insurance, so they save a bit less per dollar, about ninety-six dollars per thousand for this freelancer, but they're often much bigger. Keep both rates in mind as we go down the list.

segments.heading: Rules
segments.narration: And the rule that covers every business deduction: it has to be ordinary and necessary for your business, and you need a record. Ordinary means common in your line of work. Necessary means helpful and appropriate, not essential. A record means a receipt or bank line, plus a note on what it was for. Mixed-use things, like your phone, are deductible only for the business share. That's the whole framework. Everything below is just applying it.

segments.heading: 1 Retirement
segments.narration: Number one, by size: retirement contributions. A SEP IRA lets this freelancer put in up to about eleven thousand one hundred fifty dollars, roughly twenty percent of profit after half of self-employment tax. That cuts federal tax by about a thousand seventy dollars. A Solo four oh one k can allow more. And unlike most deductions, you keep the money. It's in your retirement account, not spent. The SEP can be opened and funded until your filing deadline, including extensions.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. a large plant pot with coins as soil. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: 2 Health
segments.narration: Number two: health insurance. If you buy your own plan and you weren't eligible for an employer's subsidized plan, including a spouse's, your premiums are generally deductible, up to your business profit. Five thousand dollars of premiums saves this freelancer about four hundred eighty dollars. If your plan is HSA-eligible, HSA contributions are deductible too, up to forty-four hundred self-only or eighty-seven fifty family for twenty twenty-six, and you can still make them for twenty twenty-six until April fifteenth.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. a medical shield with a coin. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: 3 Car
segments.narration: Number three for anyone who drives for work: the car. The standard mileage rate is seventy-two and a half cents a mile for the first half of twenty twenty-six, and seventy-six cents from July. Three thousand business miles is a deduction of about two thousand two hundred dollars, worth about five hundred dollars in tax. Parking and tolls for business trips go on top. Commuting from home to a regular workplace doesn't count. The record is a mileage log: date, where, why, miles. Without it this deduction is very hard to defend.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. a car on a curving road with mile markers. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: 4 Home office
segments.narration: Number four: the home office, if you have a space used regularly and only for business, as your main place of business. The simplified method is five dollars a square foot, up to three hundred square feet, so up to fifteen hundred dollars. The regular method uses your actual rent or mortgage interest, utilities and insurance, times the office's share of your home. For a renter with a hundred and fifty square foot office in a thousand square foot apartment, that can be close to four thousand. More records, more deduction.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. a desk inside a house outline with a tape measure. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: 5 Equipment
segments.narration: Number five: equipment. Computers, cameras, monitors, a desk. Most equipment can now be deducted in the year you start using it, rather than over several years. A two thousand dollar laptop used ninety percent for business is an eighteen hundred dollar deduction, about four hundred dollars of tax. But remember, you spent two thousand to save four hundred. Buy it because you need it, not for the deduction.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. a laptop being unboxed with a small percent tag. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: 6 Software
segments.narration: Number six: software and subscriptions. Design tools, cloud storage, accounting software, scheduling, a password manager, your website hosting and domain. Individually small, together often a thousand to three thousand dollars a year. That's worth two hundred to seven hundred in tax. The trap here is that they're spread across a dozen card statements, so freelancers miss half of them. Search your statements for every recurring charge.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. a grid of small app-like squares without logos. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: 7 Phone
segments.narration: Number seven: phone and internet, business share only. If your phone is about half business, half the bill is deductible. On a hundred dollars a month that's six hundred a year. Same idea for home internet. Pick a reasonable percentage you could explain, write down how you got it, and use it consistently. A hundred percent is hard to defend unless it's a separate business line.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. a phone and a wifi icon with a half-filled bar. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: 8 Fees
segments.narration: Number eight: fees. Payment processor fees, often about three percent of what clients pay by card, so around eighteen hundred dollars on sixty thousand. Business bank account fees. Professional memberships. The business part of tax preparation. These are easy to miss because they never feel like spending; they just quietly come out of deposits. Report gross income and list the fees.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. a coin with a small bite taken out. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: 9 Learning and travel
segments.narration: Number nine: learning and travel. Courses, books and conferences that improve skills for the work you already do. Business travel away from home overnight: flights, lodging, and fifty percent of meals. Meals with clients where you talk business are generally fifty percent deductible too. These have more rules than the others, so keep a note of who, what and why with every receipt.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. a book, a suitcase and a half-filled plate. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: 10 Contractors
segments.narration: Number ten: paying other people. If you hire a designer, an editor or a virtual assistant for your business, what you pay them is a deductible expense. If you pay any one person two thousand dollars or more directly in twenty twenty-six, you'll owe them a ten ninety-nine NEC by February first, so collect a W-9 before you pay. Advertising works the same way: ads, a portfolio site, business cards, a booth at a market. All deductible, all needing a receipt and a note.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. two small mascots shaking hands next to a megaphone. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: 11 Startup
segments.narration: Number eleven, for first-year freelancers: startup costs. Money you spent before your first client, like a course to launch, a logo, or market research, is generally deductible up to five thousand dollars in your first year, with the rest spread over fifteen years. Equipment you bought before starting is handled like other equipment once you put it to work. So if this was your first year, go back to before your first invoice and look for anything you spent to get the business going.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. a small sprouting seed next to a receipt. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Audit-proof
segments.narration: One more point before the list of things that don't count. The goal isn't the biggest possible number. It's a number you could explain calmly with paperwork. For each category, imagine handing a stranger your receipts and notes. If they'd understand what every big line was for, you're fine. If you'd need to tell a story from memory, write that story down now, while you still remember it.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. the small paper receipt mascot with a folded corner, round glasses and big eyes calmly handing a folder across a desk. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Not deductible
segments.narration: And what doesn't make the list, despite what you'll hear: your regular clothes, even nice ones you wear to meetings. Your gym. Your commute. Personal meals alone. Your entire phone bill if you use it personally. And anything bought only for the deduction. The test is simple: would you have paid for it if you didn't have the business? If yes, it's probably personal.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. a shirt, a dumbbell and a bus, all greyed out. No text, no logos, no real people.

script.title: Get your freelance taxes ready to file in one weekend
script.hook: If your freelance taxes feel like a mountain, this video is a plan to get from a messy year to ready-to-file in one weekend. Saturday, you close the books. Sunday, you check everything and either file or hand a clean package to a preparer. You'll need your bank and card statements, your forms, and about six hours in total. Twenty twenty-six returns, education, not tax advice. Let's go.

segments.heading: Intro
segments.narration: If your freelance taxes feel like a mountain, this video is a plan to get from a messy year to ready-to-file in one weekend. Saturday, you close the books. Sunday, you check everything and either file or hand a clean package to a preparer. You'll need your bank and card statements, your forms, and about six hours in total. Twenty twenty-six returns, education, not tax advice. Let's go.
segments.on_screen_text: Ready to file in one weekend
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. the small paper receipt mascot with a folded corner, round glasses and big eyes with a weekend calendar, a coffee cup and a folder. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Prep
segments.narration: Friday night, ten minutes of prep. Download twelve months of statements for every account that touched business money: business checking, any card you used for business, PayPal or Stripe, and your personal account if business money ever landed there. Download every ten ninety-nine you've received. Log in to your IRS Online Account and screenshot your twenty twenty-six estimated payments. Put it all in one folder. That's it for Friday. If you use accounting software or our tracker, export its reports too. And make a simple notes file where you'll write down every judgment call you make this weekend, like a business percentage or a rebuilt mileage entry, so you can explain it later.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. a laptop with files sliding into one folder. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Sat 1 Income
segments.narration: Saturday morning, block one: income. Go through every deposit in your business accounts and tag it: client payment, transfer from yourself, refund, or other. Add client payments by client. Then compare each client's total to their ten ninety-nine, if they sent one. Differences are usually timing or fees. Write a one-line note for each difference. Your income total is the sum of client payments actually received in twenty twenty-six, gross of fees.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. a ledger with rows grouped by color. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Sat 2 Expenses
segments.narration: Block two: expenses. Go through every outgoing line and tag the business ones with a category: software, equipment, fees, phone and internet, travel, meals, education, office supplies, contractors, advertising, and so on. If a purchase was mixed use, tag the business percentage. Anything you can't explain in a few words, leave untagged rather than guessing. Then total each category. This block takes the longest, so put on music.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. colored folders being filled with receipts. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Sat 3 Gaps
segments.narration: Block three, after lunch: gaps. Look for business expenses paid from your personal account, things like a domain renewal on your personal card. Add those. Look for cash expenses, like parking. Add those with a note. Look for anything in the business account that was actually personal, and take it out of expenses. This is where mixing accounts costs you time, and it's the best argument for keeping them separate this year.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. two account icons with an arrow moving a coin between them. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Messy year
segments.narration: If your records are a real mess, don't let it stop you. Rebuild what you can from bank and card statements, invoices you sent, client emails and your calendar. Those are records too. Where you truly can't find proof, leave it out rather than guessing. A slightly higher tax bill is better than a deduction you can't support. And promise yourself one change for this year, like a separate business card, so next January is easier.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. the small paper receipt mascot with a folded corner, round glasses and big eyes piecing together torn paper pieces. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Sat 4 Miles
segments.narration: Block four: miles and home. Total your business miles from your log. You'll also need total miles driven, so use your odometer photos from January and December, or service records. If your log has holes, rebuild it from your calendar and client addresses, and be honest. Then the home office, if you qualify: measure the office and your home, and if you're using the regular method, total rent or mortgage interest, utilities and renter's or homeowner's insurance.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. a dashboard odometer and a tape measure. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Sat 5 Benefits
segments.narration: Last block on Saturday: benefits. Total your health insurance premiums for the year from the insurer's statements or your marketplace form, the ten ninety-five A if you used healthcare.gov. Total any HSA contributions. And decide on retirement: if you want a SEP IRA contribution for twenty twenty-six, work out the amount now, because it changes your return. You can make it later, up to your filing deadline, but decide the number before you file.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. a medical shield and a plant pot. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Sun 1 Numbers
segments.narration: Sunday morning, put the numbers together. Income minus expenses gives your Schedule C profit. Run it through our free calculator or your tracker to estimate your total federal tax. Compare that with the estimated payments you made. The difference is roughly what you'll owe or get back. Now check it against your tax savings account. If it's short, you know now, in January, not on April fourteenth.
segments.on_screen_text: Sun 9am: profit → tax → owe or refund
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. a simple equation made of coin stacks. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Sun 2 Sanity
segments.narration: Then a sanity check, because this is where errors hide. Is your profit within about ten percent of what you expected? Are the forms' totals covered by your income, or explained? Are any expense categories unusually large compared with last year? Big round numbers with no receipts are what draw questions, so make sure each big one has paperwork. And make sure all four estimated payments are on your list, including the January one. Finally, look at last year's return side by side. Anything that changed a lot should have a reason you can say in one sentence.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. a magnifying glass over a ledger. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Sun 3 File
segments.narration: Sunday afternoon: file or hand off. If you're using software, go through it now with your numbers ready; with clean totals most freelancers finish in a couple of hours. If you use a preparer, send them a single, organized package: the income summary by client, the forms, expenses by category, miles, home office details, health and retirement numbers, estimated payments, and last year's return. Clean packages cost less to prepare.
segments.on_screen_text: Sun 1pm: file or send the package
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. a neat folder going into an envelope. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Can't pay
segments.narration: What if the numbers show you'll owe more than you have? File on time anyway. The penalty for not filing is about ten times the penalty for not paying: five percent a month versus half a percent. Pay as much as you can by April fifteenth. Then look at the IRS's online payment plans. For balances under certain limits you can set one up online in minutes, with lower fees than a credit card. Interest still runs, so pay it off as fast as you can, but it's manageable.
segments.on_screen_text: Can't pay? File anyway + payment plan
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. a calendar with a row of small coins stretching across months. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: State
segments.narration: Don't forget your state return, if your state has an income tax. Most software carries the numbers over. Most states use your federal profit as the starting point, then add their own adjustments, and some cities, like New York City, have their own tax on top. Check whether you made state estimated payments too, because those go on the state return, not the federal one.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. a map outline next to a second form. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Refund
segments.narration: And if you're getting a refund, that means you paid more than you owed during the year. Nice, but it's also money you lent the government for free. You can ask for it back, or apply it to your first twenty twenty-seven estimated payment. Either is fine; just choose on purpose and write down which one you picked.
segments.on_screen_text: Refund: take it or apply to 2027
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. a coin boomeranging back to a hand. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Timing
segments.narration: One timing note. If any forms are still missing or you're waiting on brokerage statements, do everything except the final submit, then file once they arrive. You don't need to file the first day the IRS opens. You do need to pay any balance by April fifteenth. And if you'll owe, you can file now and schedule the payment for April, so the money earns interest in your savings for a few more months.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. a calendar with a scheduled coin on April 15. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Next year
segments.narration: Before you close the laptop, set up next year so this weekend is shorter. Your twenty twenty-six total tax is now your safe harbor for twenty twenty-seven. Divide it by four, and that's each quarterly payment if you choose that method. Work out your new set-aside percentage. And start a monthly ten-minute check-in to tag transactions as you go, so next January takes one afternoon instead of a weekend.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. a new calendar page with four coral dots. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Recap
segments.narration: Recap: Friday, download everything. Saturday, income by client, expenses by category, fill the gaps, miles and home office, then health and retirement. Sunday, profit and tax, sanity check, then file or hand off a clean package. Pay by April fifteenth, and set up twenty twenty-seven while it's fresh.
